```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer, and A has better evidence that people pay. AltText.ai offers paid tiers from $5 to $59 a month and has 142 reviews since 2023. Gelo.ai and Fyvello also list live paid plans. B's price anchors come from products that are pre-launch, waitlist-only, or have undisclosed prices. So B shows no confirmed transaction in its category.",
    "A asks the buyer for far less trust. A merchant approving an app to write product copy is a small ask. B needs startups to give a solo stranger PR-opening access to production code. B's own brief says SOC 2 Type II or equivalent is commonly expected and likely out of scope for a 6-week build.",
    "B faces free substitutes of its core function. Nalvis is an open-source GitHub Action, mendapi is AGPL and free, and ApiPatch is on PyPI. A's competitors also have free tiers, but A's brief documents paid tiers existing alongside them. B's brief documents no proven paid tier.",
    "A's weaknesses are about discovery and margins: saturated App Store rankings, entry prices of $5 to $12.90, and about $500/month of ads for 90 days. These make scaling hard but do not block a first sale. B's trust and compliance barrier blocks the first sale directly.",
    "B's demand quotes are weaker than they look. At least one comes from a builder promoting their own fix ('how I built a fix'). A's quotes include a review of a paid app, which ties the pain to payment."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's price hypothesis of $14–150/mo. The $14 anchor is Nalvis's hosted tier, which the brief itself describes as pre-launch/waitlist. Since.dev's Pro price is undisclosed, mendapi's hosted tier has no price, and Ripple, Sync, and api-guardian pricing is NOT FOUND. Only Since.dev's $149 Studio tier is a published price, and nothing shows anyone paying it.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's case has its own gaps. The 473-review incumbent it leans on runs a free plan, so those reviews do not prove payment. The claim of 0% Shopify revenue share under $1M/year has no URL. The 'industry commentary' on photo-only quality has no URL. The ads-payback evidence comes from a single agency case study. A's path to a first customer is probably slow and expensive through a crowded App Store. B loses mainly because its briefs show no paid transactions and a heavy trust/compliance barrier, not because its demand is fake."
}
```
